version.changelog:
- Initial release of the x-twitter API skill.
- Provides scripts to search tweets, retrieve article/tweet content, and fetch trending topics from X (Twitter).
- Supports Bearer Token and OAuth 2.0 authentication.
- Includes usage examples, advanced query operators, and output/export options.
- Handles API errors and rate limits with automatic retry logic.
- Detailed setup and API limit information included in documentation.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: small Python scripts that call X (Twitter) API endpoints, requiring only python3 and a single X_BEARER_TOKEN, with no unexpected installs or unrelated credential access.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (search tweets, get articles, trends) match the included scripts and requested binary (python3). The primary credential X_BEARER_TOKEN is exactly what's needed to call the X API; no unrelated credentials or binaries are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the scripts only instruct running the three Python scripts that call api.x.com endpoints, parse results, print and optionally save them. There are no instructions to read unrelated files, other environment variables, or to exfiltrate data to third-party endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec — instruction-only with bundled scripts. No downloads, no archive extraction, and no package installs referenced in SKILL.md, so there is minimal install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only a single sensitive env var (X_BEARER_TOKEN) is required and it's appropriate for the stated functionality. The scripts only read that token and do not reference other secrets or config paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled, does not request persistent system-wide changes, and does not modify other skills' configurations. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal) but nothing in the skill implies elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: run the Python scripts to call the X API. Before installing/use: (1) Only provide a bearer token with minimum required scope and avoid embedding long-lived secrets in shared shell config if you don't trust the environment. (2) Run the scripts in a sandbox if you want to verify network activity; they call https://api.x.com only. (3) Be aware trending endpoints may require a paid tier per the README. (4) If you need stronger assurance, review the included Python code (small and readable) or run it with a throwaway token first.
